cards.ja: メキシコ風の甘いパン
朝食がすばらしかったとお伝えしたいです。
cards.glossEn: I want to tell you that the breakfast was wonderful.

cards.ja: コーヒーはおいしくて、ちょうど私好みでした。
cards.glossEn: The coffee was delicious and exactly to my taste.

cards.ja: とてもやわらかかったので、すごく気に入りました。
cards.glossEn: Because it was very soft, I liked it very much.

cards.ja: 接客していただき、本当にありがとうございました。
cards.glossEn: Thank you very much for serving me.

cards.ja: 明日また来たら、もう一つ注文します。
cards.glossEn: If I come again tomorrow, I will order one more.

reader.ja: 旅行者の女性は、小さなカフェで朝食を食べ終え、料理人と話したいと思っています。
reader.glossEn: A female traveler finishes her breakfast at a small café and wants to talk with the cook.

reader.ja: 彼女は彼にあいさつをして言います。「朝食がすばらしかったとお伝えしたいです。」
reader.glossEn: She greets him and says: 'I want to tell you that the breakfast was wonderful.'

reader.ja: 「コーヒーはとても濃くて、香りがすばらしく、ちょうど私好みでした。」
reader.glossEn: The coffee was very strong, its aroma was wonderful, and it was exactly to my taste.

reader.ja: 「甘いパンは中はやわらかく、外はカリッとしていて、甘すぎませんでした。」
reader.glossEn: The sweet bread was soft inside, crisp outside, and not too sweet.

reader.ja: 「卵もクリーミーで味つけがとてもよかったので、すごく気に入りました。」
reader.glossEn: I also liked the eggs very much because they were creamy and very well seasoned.

reader.ja: 料理人はにっこり笑って、その甘いパンは自分の祖母のレシピだと説明します。
reader.glossEn: The cook smiles and explains that the sweet bread is his grandmother's recipe.

reader.ja: 旅行者は彼に言います。「明日また来たら、あのパンをもう一つ注文します。」
reader.glossEn: The traveler tells him: 'If I come again tomorrow, I will order one more of that bread.'

reader.ja: 店を出る前に、彼女はカウンターにチップを置き、スタッフに接客のお礼を言います。
reader.glossEn: Before leaving the shop, she places a tip on the counter and thanks the staff for the service.

reader.ja: 料理人は答えます。「どうもありがとうございます。気に入っていただけて、私たちはとてもうれしいです。」
reader.glossEn: The cook answers: 'Thank you very much. We are very glad you liked it.'

issues: The source is a Mexican café scene. Keep pan dulce and the tip on the counter as scene facts; qualified Japanese and Mexican-food review should check メキシコ風の甘いパン as a descriptive label.
Card 13 and Reader 2 render a direct compliment as 朝食がすばらしかった; qualified Japanese review should decide the most natural customer-to-cook phrasing.
The term 接客 covers service in this café context but is narrower than all uses of Spanish atención; dictionary review should pin the sense.
Card 18 says another one without a referent, as the source card does; Reader 7 names the bread. Preserve this card/Reader difference until source review.
The source note felicitarlo/felicitarla is a Spanish gender contrast. It is internal source context, not a Japanese form rule.
